points: The Q3 2026 print will show whether KNX hit the $0.71-$0.77 adjusted EPS guidance issued with Q2 and whether the pricing acceleration and insurance/brokerage cost reset that management described actually flowed through the quarter.

It will also reveal if truckload market tightening continued through the summer; reports suggest management cited rapid TL tightening and accelerating fundamentals in Q2, so Q3 rate and utilization trends will test whether the cycle inflection is durable.

The setup for the following quarters depends on Q3 pricing gains sticking: consensus already expects FY1 EPS of $2.31 and FY2 EPS of $4.00, implying roughly 84% then 73% growth, so a Q3 beat would likely pull FY2 estimates higher and make the 0.36 PEG look cheap versus the theme.

Estimate momentum is already behind the name, with 90-day revenue revisions up 23.65% and 16 up/0 down analyst moves in the past 30 days; the print will show whether that momentum is backed by fundamentals or has gotten ahead of itself.

KNX reports before most peers, with JBHT, ARCB, ODFL, MRTN and HTLD following over the next two weeks; KNX’s Q4 commentary and early 2027 outlook will set the read-through for the group and either reinforce or challenge the theme’s active long lean.

Valuation is flagged as fair at 0.8x theme P/E and 0.7x theme PEG, so the long case rests on earnings acceleration rather than multiple expansion; the print needs to confirm that the cost reset and firmer rate environment can deliver the consensus EPS trajectory.
watch: Q3 adjusted EPS versus the $0.71-$0.77 guidance — a print at or above the high end supports the long.
Truckload pricing/rate-per-mile trend — continued acceleration supports the long.
Insurance and brokerage cost reset progress — lower expense drag or margin improvement supports the long.
FY2 EPS revision direction after the print — upward moves from the $4.00 consensus support the long.
